question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ -6 \\ -11\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ -6 \\ -11\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1} \\ 5{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ -6 \\ -11\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ -6 \\ -11\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-6 \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-11\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $3$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}13{x}_{2} &=-39 \\ {x}_{2} &=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=-3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ -{x}_{1}+4(-3) &=-11 \\ -{x}_{1} &=1 \\ {x}_{1} &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=-3$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ 5(-1)+2(-3) &=-11 \\ -11 &=-11\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=-3$, which means

$$
-{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2}=d.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-1)+(-3)=-4.
$$
